notes: TBox rule edit: the definition of a fjord (a sea-flooded glacial valley) is swapped for that of a ria (a sea-flooded river valley), its closest real neighbour, so the counterfactual is plausible. Derivability very_unlikely: the definition is stated directly and follows from nothing. No real exceptions: a fjord is glacial by definition. New members named in the prompt (Hvalfjörður, Tunulliarfik) are obscure, so the rule is their only route: determinate. Well-known members Milford Sound and Doubtful Sound are both called 'Sound' though they are fjords, which makes the world where they stop counting as fjords reasonable. The two background queries ask well-known members whose property a model likely also stores by name (README, TBox). For each member, one world keeps the stored property and the member stops counting as a member of the class; the other keeps the membership and applies the edited rule. The two members' choices are independent, so the worlds combine them (four). Lopsided worlds are kept (README Decisions 4). The either-or questions take one value for granted; since 2026-10-31 this is stated as a bridge of the two well-known-member queries ('A valley carved by a glacier was not carved by a river.'), which is why each world gives up either the membership or the stored value (formal check, FINDINGS B3/C3).
